mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate compresses discount rates for equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as capital costs fall.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are negative in > 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines for 3 months, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 10.0% within a 3-month window, it signals deepening recessionary stress, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as risk aversion surges.
failure_condition: SPX 5d returns are positive in > 40% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 10.0% for 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous 3-month decline in housing starts (HOUST) and GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates weakening consumer demand, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days due to earnings contraction expectations.
candidate_trigger: HOUST declines > 5% and GDPC1 declines > 1% in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are positive in > 40% of instances when both HOUST and GDPC1 decline as specified.

mechanism_narrative: During industrial production contraction (INDPRO < 90), the S&P 500 underperforms with negative returns over 60 days as manufacturing weakness signals broad economic slowdown and earnings deterioration.
failure_condition: SPX 60d returns are positive in > 50% of periods when INDPRO < 90 for 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in retail sales (RSAFS) signals strong consumer demand, supporting positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days through elevated corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are negative in > 60% of periods when RSAFS increases for 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: When year-over-year CPI rises above 3.0% within a 3-month window, accelerating inflation triggers negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days due to anticipated Federal Reserve policy tightening.
failure_condition: SPX 5d returns are positive in > 40% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0% YoY for 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous 3-month decline in payrolls (PAYEMS) and rise in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates labor market deterioration, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days as consumer spending weakens.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS declines > 1% and UNRATE rises > 0.5% in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are positive in > 40% of instances when both PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises as specified.

mechanism_narrative: In high unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 9.5%), the S&P 500 typically produces negative returns over 60 days as economic recovery remains slow and corporate earnings face persistent headwinds.
failure_condition: SPX 60d returns are positive in > 50% of periods when UNRATE > 9.5% for 3 months.
